ui.plugins.google.howtoTitle: How to get the secret address
ui.plugins.google.howto1: Open Google Calendar on the web on a computer, click the gear at the top right → Settings
ui.plugins.google.howto2: Under "Settings for my calendars" on the left, pick the calendar to sync and scroll to "Integrate calendar"
ui.plugins.google.howto3: Copy the "Secret address in iCal format" and paste it above
ui.plugins.google.howtoSafe: This address works like a password — anyone with it can see your calendar. Ergo only keeps it in this computer's secrets area. If it leaks, click "Reset" in the same place and enter the new address here
ui.plugins.google.gmail.addressChange: Use a different Gmail address (leave empty to keep it)
ui.plugins.google.gmail.howtoTitle: How to create an app password
ui.plugins.google.gmail.howto1: Open the Security page of your Google account (myaccount.google.com/security) and turn on 2-Step Verification first
ui.plugins.google.gmail.howto2: Then open the App passwords page (myaccount.google.com/apppasswords; you can also search for "App passwords" on the Security page), give it a name (like "Ergo") and click Create
ui.plugins.google.gmail.howto3: Copy the 16-letter password into the box above along with your Gmail address, then click Connect and test
ui.plugins.google.gmail.readOnly: Read-only: Ergo only searches and reads mail; it never sends, deletes or changes read status, and received mail isn't stored. Only with Import on does it turn the mail you send into material
ui.plugins.google.gmail.safe: This password can read your whole mailbox: Ergo keeps it only in this computer's secrets area and never shows it on pages or in logs. To stop, delete it on Google's App passwords page and click Disconnect here
ui.plugins.google.gmail.revoked: Changing your Google account password revokes all app passwords; create a new one and enter it here
ui.plugins.google.gmail.missing: No "App passwords" option? Google doesn't offer it when 2-Step Verification uses only security keys, for work or school accounts, or with Advanced Protection

ui.plugins.phone.brings.photosLocation: "Connect album" and "Start recording location" in Settings · Data sources, and sending photo times/places and recorded locations while the app is open
ui.plugins.phone.photos.notInApp: Open this page in the Ergo app on your phone to connect the album; once connected, the app reads the times and places of photos from the last few days every 30 minutes while it's open.
ui.plugins.phone.photos.granted: Ergo may read the album and photo locations
ui.plugins.phone.photos.grantedNoLocatio: Ergo may read the album but not photo locations (photos have no places)
ui.plugins.phone.photos.denied: Ergo isn't allowed to read the album (denied or revoked)
ui.plugins.phone.photos.power: Battery: only reads the times and places of photos while the app is open (on open, when coming back, every 30 minutes), never the photos themselves — barely any battery.
ui.plugins.phone.photos.privacy: Privacy: photos never leave the phone; only when and where they were taken go to Ergo on your own computer. The raw times and places are kept in Ergo's data directory and can be cleared by day below. Each day becomes one summary in memory; places count as "location", a sensitive category, so they're left out while location inference is off. Place names come from your phone's system turning coordinates into names (the coordinates go to the phone's map service, e.g. Huawei); if it can't, a latitude/longitude area is used. Frequent places you named under "Phone · Location" use their names.
ui.plugins.phone.photos.deniedNow: No permission to read the album, so it isn't connected. You can turn on Photos in the phone's Settings · Apps · Ergo · Permissions, then tap "Connect album" again.

ui.plugins.phone.photos.skipped.import_o: Import for "Phone · Photo times and places" is off
ui.plugins.phone.photos.skipped.already_: Permission is still off: sync again after turning it on in the phone's settings
ui.plugins.phone.location.notInApp: Open this page in the Ergo app on your phone to start recording location; location only exists from the moment recording starts, nothing earlier.
ui.plugins.phone.location.background: Also record when the app is in the background
ui.plugins.phone.location.backgroundSub: A notification saying a location task is running stays on (dismissing it goes back to recording only while the app is open); uses more battery
ui.plugins.phone.location.denied: Ergo isn't allowed to use location (denied or revoked)
ui.plugins.phone.location.switchOff: set to record, but the phone's location switch is off: turn on Location in the control center or settings
ui.plugins.phone.location.switchOffReaso: The phone's location switch is off, so no location is recorded: turn on Location in the control center or settings
ui.plugins.phone.location.power: Battery: while the app is open it records a point every 5 minutes with low-power positioning (Wi-Fi and cell towers, no GPS); HarmonyOS suspends the app a few seconds after it goes to the background, so nothing is recorded then. With "Also record when the app is in the background" on, a HarmonyOS location continuous task records every 10 minutes in the background with a notification always shown — more battery (how much depends on the device).
ui.plugins.phone.location.privacy: Privacy: raw points are first kept on the phone and sent to Ergo on your own computer while the app is open, kept in Ergo's data directory and clearable by day below. Each day becomes one summary of where you went and how long you stayed; the whole entry counts as "location", a sensitive category, so it isn't used for inference while location inference is off. Place names come from your phone's system turning coordinates into names (the coordinates go to the phone's map service, e.g. Huawei); if it can't, a latitude/longitude area is used. Frequent places you named use their names.
ui.plugins.phone.location.deniedNow: No location permission, so recording didn't start. You can turn on Location in the phone's Settings · Apps · Ergo · Permissions, then tap "Start recording location" again.
